methodology: The original research topic and the generated technical specification were decomposed into atomic units based on individual requirements, features, behaviors, and constraints. Each atomic unit is designed to be independent, self-contained, technically specific, unambiguous, and implementable as a single requirement. This ensures a granular comparison between the two sets of information.
mindtraced_atomic_units: Counter counts from 0000 to 9999 and wraps around
ena[1] is the enable signal for the tens digit
ena[2] is the enable signal for the hundreds digit
ena[3] is the enable signal for the thousands digit
Ones digit increments every clock cycle when not reset
Counter resets to 0000 when the reset input is high
spec_atomic_units: clk input is the clock signal
reset is the synchronous active-high reset signal
ena[3:1] are the enable signals for the tens, hundreds, and thousands digits respectively
q[15:0] is the 16-bit output representing the four BCD digits
ena[1] is asserted when the ones digit (q[3:0]) is equal to 9
ena[2] is asserted when both the ones digit (q[3:0]) and the tens digit (q[7:4]) are equal to 9
ena[3] is asserted when the ones digit (q[3:0]), the tens digit (q[7:4]), and the hundreds digit (q[11:8]) are all equal to 9
Output q[15:0] is a direct concatenation of the four BCD digits
Counter increments on rising edge of clk when reset is low
When reset is high, counter synchronously resets to 0 on the next rising edge of clk
ena signals indicate when the corresponding digit should be incremented on the next clock cycle
Design uses four 4-bit registers (ones, tens, hundreds, thousands) to store the BCD digits
Registers are reset to 0 only on the rising edge of the clock when the reset signal is high
